I added a static helper, RowGroupCollection::GetParallelScanMorselVectors(total_rows, row_group_size, threads). It aims for about 4 morsels per thread, uses at least 4 vectors (8k rows) per morsel, and never more than one row group. RowGroupCollection::NextParallelScan now uses the existing sub-row-group branch whenever the morsel is smaller than the current row group, or when it is part-way through a row group. That branch was previously only used under verify_parallelism, which still gets 1 vector. It advances vector_index by the morsel size and adds the morsel's own rows to processed_rows. DataTable::MaxThreads uses the same helper, so the scan source starts enough threads. I put the helper in row_group_collection.hpp rather than scan_state.hpp, so ParallelCollectionScanState is unchanged. The morsel size is recomputed under the lock on every call, which is a few arithmetic operations. structured_output.summary: Parallel table scans can now hand out pieces of a row group (morsels) instead of always handing out a whole row group (~122k rows) per task. I added a static helper, RowGroupCollection::GetParallelScanMorselVectors(total_rows, row_group_size, threads). It aims for about 4 morsels per thread, uses at least 4 vectors (8k rows) per morsel, and never more than one row group. RowGroupCollection::NextParallelScan now uses the existing sub-row-group branch whenever the morsel is smaller than the current row group, or when it is part-way through a row group. That branch was previously only used under verify_parallelism, which still gets 1 vector. It advances vector_index by the morsel size and adds the morsel's own rows to processed_rows. DataTable::MaxThreads uses the same helper, so the scan source starts enough threads. I put the helper in row_group_collection.hpp rather than scan_state.hpp, so ParallelCollectionScanState is unchanged. The morsel size is recomputed under the lock on every call, which is a few arithmetic operations. Results: the build is OK and bench reported no result mismatches. q02 went from 88.7 to 72.3 ms (-18.5%) on the first run and from 91.2 to 79.0 ms (-13.4%) on the second. Before the change, the profile showed the 100k-row supplier scan taking 0.02s on a single thread.
structured_output.generality: This helps any parallel scan of a table with few row groups compared with the thread count. That covers dimension or small tables (under about thread_count*4*60 vectors, roughly 4M rows at 8 threads) with wide string columns or expensive filters, which often feed hash-join builds, CTEs or small aggregations. It also improves load balance when the row-group count is not a multiple of the thread count. Large tables are unchanged, because the morsel size reaches the row-group size and the old whole-row-group path is used. Very small tables (under about 8k rows) still produce one morsel.
structured_output.notes:
- MaxThreads uses GetTotalRows(), while NextParallelScan uses max_row minus the base row id fixed at scan start. The two can differ slightly if rows are appended during a scan, but that only affects the thread-count estimate, not correctness.
- Under verify_parallelism, processed_rows is now updated as well; before, it was never updated in that mode.
- Not measured in isolation: whether scanning from a vector offset inside compressed or FSST string segments costs extra. The end-to-end time improved anyway.
- Possible follow-ups: tune MORSELS_PER_THREAD and MIN_MORSEL_VECTORS, and check that the 17-row-group part scan (now about 31-vector morsels) is balanced.
